messages:
sam: Heads-up: customer ops flagged that a set of tenants were billed at free-tier rates for ~45m yesterday despite having upgraded plans. ledger raw shows tokens marked with plan_id 'free' while plan service shows them upgraded. anywhere else seeing plan-override cache activity?
jules: I looked — there was a churny batch of plan updates around 18:10 UTC and the routing plan-override cache (sharded local LRU) had a small eviction storm. some shards fell back to reading stale defaults (free) while updates propagated asynchronously
mia: so edge emitted metering events with plan_id=free during the window? that would explain undercharge in previews and ledger deltas
sam: yes. events look otherwise normal, just the plan_id dimension wrong. aggregator groups pricing by plan_id so mislabeling flows straight into invoices
omar: why does the cache exist locally? I thought we relied on plan-service pub/sub for immediate consistency
jules: historical reason: plan-service pub/sub had outage risk causing throttle spikes on the edge. so we introduced a sharded, eventually-consistent override cache with 5s TTL and async refresh. normally works, but with high fanout of updates it got overwhelmed and some shards returned default 'free' if lookup failed
kevin: we need to decide short-term mitigation vs long-term architecture change. Short-term: have edge include plan_epoch/version and read-through fallback: on cache miss, call plan-service synchronously for that tenant (slow path) and annotate event with plan_epoch. Long-term: make plan-service publish versioned plan snapshots and require events to carry plan_epoch so aggregator can pick latest-known plan for a given event window
mia: good call. if events include plan_epoch we can do a reconciliation step: when aggregator sees a later plan_epoch for same tenant/time-window, it can reprice or emit correction events. that allows eventual consistency without losing correctness
sam: proposal: (1) edge change: attach plan_epoch (int timestamp) on metering events; on local cache miss, call plan-service sync and attach plan_epoch and a header plan_miss=true (for telemetry) (2) aggregator change: add logic to prefer highest plan_epoch within invoice window and emit correction lines if repricing occurs (3) console: add per-tenant "plan_epoch_applied" column in invoice preview and a flag if repriced post-facto (4) backfill job: find windows where ledger differed from plan-service history during spike and emit corrections
omar: implementation caveats: plan-service sync calls at edge under heavy load could increase tail latency. need to limit sync calls via token bucket and sample heavy tenants rather than all. maybe only sync on first event for tenant within a glue-window and rely on async refresh after that
jules: alternate lighter approach: keep local cache but add a short-lived negative cache key so we don't return default on transient failures; and emit missing_plan=true metric so we can alert the moment the cache returns default. but this won't fix already-mis-emitted events
kevin: I prefer the plan_epoch approach because it's additive and gives us authoritative reconciliation path. We need to ensure epoch is monotonic and assigned by plan-service at update time. Also define TTL semantics: aggregator must only consider plan_epochs within X minutes of event timestamp to avoid resurrecting ancient plan changes
mia: ops checklist draft: 1) plan-service: add plan_epoch on update events and expose sync lookup API returning (plan_id, epoch) 2) edge: include plan_epoch in metering event (canary + feature flag) 3) aggregator: prefer max(plan_epoch) for a given tenant/window and emit repricing correction if changed 4) console: surface plan_epoch and repriced lines in invoice preview 5) backfill: detection script to find affected windows and reprice ledger rows 6) alerts: missing_plan_rate, plan_epoch_mismatch_rate, repriced_events_rate
sam: canary proposal: 2h on a small cohort (15 tenants) across regions. enable plan_epoch header only for cohort. monitor plan_miss telemetry and invoice deltas. start 02:30 UTC tomorrow. I'll own cohort and validation queries
omar: I'll own plan-service changes and a throttled sync endpoint. make sure we instrument rate and latency on sync path
jules: I'll handle cache tweaks and negative-key strategy as interim safety net. also add dashboard card "plan_cache_miss_rate by shard"
kevin: aggregator work: add repricing pipeline and tombstone/correction emit. Also add an audit table for plan_epoch changes per window to make backfills easier
ops-bot: Ticket MET-7007 created by sam: "billing: plan-override cache evictions caused free-tier misattribution; attach plan_epoch to metering events and add repricing path". priority P1. owners: sam (canary & validation), omar (plan-service), jules (edge cache), kevin (aggregator), mia (console). ETA: canary tomorrow 02:30 UTC
mia: console UX: show small badge "repriced" with hover text "tokens re-priced due to plan update propagation; see MET-7007" when correction events applied. also surface pre/post totals so support can explain changes
sam: tests: unit tests for epoch ordering, integration load test for plan-service sync under sampled traffic, staging end-to-end with simulated eviction storm to ensure repricing triggers corrections
omar: note: ensure plan_epoch is signed/trusted to prevent tampering in events. use short HMAC with plan-service key when attaching epoch if needed for security-sensitive tenants
jules: I'll also add a temporary rule: if missing plan_epoch and cache returned default recently, emit high-severity alert so we can stop rollout quickly next time
ops-bot: MET-7007 updated: owners and canary schedule. reminder scheduled for canary 02:30 UTC tomorrow
